title: The Commandments — The Law Fulfilled

The Law Fulfilled

This page preserves the numbered Christ studies and their quoted passages. Open the complementary Harmony study. The two views serve different purposes; their entry counts are not added together.

Additional study mark: Transformed explains a changed covenant practice and the continuing response in The Way. Browse the 20 marked entries.

Verified Saints Translation links. Biblical references open the Saints chapter at its exact verse anchor. Saints numbering appears first; corresponding KJV numbers are shown where they differ. Ranges open at their first verse. Read the citation and numbering notes.

The Commandments of Christ · The commandments of Moses as Christ takes them up · 1–28

← Index of the Law by verse  ·  The Commandments of Christ: all subjects  ·  Repent, Believe, Follow →

Jesus did not come to abolish the Law or the Prophets but to fulfil them. Here are the places where He takes up a commandment of Moses, names it, and carries it to its root: from the deed to the heart, from the letter to the will of the Father. Each entry includes links to the relevant Torah study or biblical passage.

Fulfillment and faithful response. The Torah entries now distinguish fulfillment, Christ’s teaching, apostolic application and original covenant setting. The commands of Christ below remain calls to hear and do his teaching. Explore the fulfillment marks, biblical evidence and Christian responses.

On this page: The Law and the Prophets · You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You · Marriage · The Sabbath · Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders · The Commandments and the One Thing Lacking · Temple, Offerings and Tithes · Done to Be Seen

The Law and the Prophets

1. Not to suppose that He came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; to do and teach even the least of these commandments, with a righteousness greater than that of the scribes and Pharisees.

Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish, but to fulfil. For truly I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota nor one stroke shall pass from the Law, until all things come to pass. Whoever therefore loosens one of these least commandments and teaches people to do so shall be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does and teaches them shall be called great in the kingdom of the heavens. For I tell you: unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you shall by no means enter the kingdom of the heavens.

Matthew 5:17–20

See also: Luke 16:17
In the Law: 108. Preserving the instruction God gives

2. The first commandment of all: to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength.

Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one. You shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, with your whole soul, with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.’

Mark 12:29–30

See also: Matthew 22:37–38
In the Law: 111. Loving God wholeheartedly

3. The second, like it: to love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets.

A second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets.”

Matthew 22:39–40

See also: Mark 12:31 · Luke 10:27–28
In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

4. To do to others whatever you wish them to do to you, for this is the Law and the Prophets.

So in everything, whatever you wish people to do for you, you also do likewise for them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.

Matthew 7:12

See also: Luke 6:31
In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

You Heard That It Was Said, but I Tell You

5. Murder: whoever is angry with his brother, insults him or calls him a fool is liable to judgment.

You have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not murder’; and ‘whoever murders shall be liable to judgment.’ But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother shall be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca,’ shall be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ shall be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

Matthew 5:21–22

In the Law: 24. The prohibition of murder · 77. Rejecting hatred of a brother

6. To be reconciled with your brother before you bring your gift to the altar, and to come to terms quickly with your accuser.

If therefore you offer your gift upon the altar, and there remember that your brother has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar, and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift. Come to terms with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way, lest your adversary hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.

Matthew 5:23–25

See also: Luke 12:58
In the Law: 24. The prohibition of murder

7. Adultery: whoever looks at a woman to desire her has already committed adultery in his heart; better to lose an eye or a hand than to be thrown into Gehenna.

You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall not commit adultery.’ But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart. If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna. And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.

Matthew 5:27–30

See also: Matthew 18:8–9 · Mark 9:43–47
In the Law: 25. Faithfulness in marriage · 28. Rejecting covetous desire

Textual note: The parallel Mark 9:43–47 spans verses 44 and 46, which are absent from the current Saints main text; open the chapter for its textual notes.

8. Divorce: whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery.

And it was said: ‘Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.’ But I tell you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, causes her to commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

Matthew 5:31–32

See also: Luke 16:18
In the Law: 149. Divorce regulation and Jesus’ teaching

9. Oaths: not to swear at all; let your word be Yes, yes, or No, no.

Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old: ‘You shall not swear falsely, but shall fulfil your oaths to the Lord.’ But I tell you: do not swear at all, neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God, nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of His feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black. But let your word be ‘Yes, yes’; ‘No, no.’ Whatever is beyond these is of evil.

Matthew 5:33–37

See also: Matthew 23:16–22
In the Law: 21. Honoring God’s name in speech and life · 120. Oaths by God’s name and Jesus’ instruction · 107. Vows, responsibility and household rules

10. An eye for an eye: not to resist the evil person; to turn the other cheek, give the cloak also, go the second mile, and give to the one who asks.

You have heard that it was said: ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’ But I tell you: do not resist the evildoer; but whoever strikes you upon your right cheek, turn the other to him also. And if anyone would sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak also. And whoever compels you to go one Roman mile, go with him two. Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who would borrow from you.

Matthew 5:38–42

See also: Luke 6:29–30
In the Law: 100. Proportionate justice and Jesus’ teaching on retaliation · 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

11. Love of neighbor: to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so as to be sons of your Father in the heavens; to be perfect as He is perfect.

You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.’ But I tell you: love your enemies, and pray for those who persecute you, that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens; for He makes His sun rise upon the evil and the good, and sends rain upon the righteous and the unrighteous. For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing beyond others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same? You shall therefore be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

Matthew 5:43–48

See also: Luke 6:27–28 · Luke 6:32–36
In the Law: 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

Marriage

12. What God has yoked together, no human being is to separate. Moses permitted divorce because of hardness of heart, but from the beginning it was not so.

He answered, “Have you not read that the Creator from the beginning made them male and female, and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has yoked together, let no human being separate.” They said to Him, “Why then did Moses command giving a certificate of divorce and divorcing her?” He said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart Moses permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so. I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on account of sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery.”

Matthew 19:4–9

See also: Mark 10:5–12
In the Law: 6. Marriage and the one-flesh union · 149. Divorce regulation and Jesus’ teaching

The Sabbath

13. The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath. The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.

He said to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and hungry, he and those with him: how he entered God’s house in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which only priests may lawfully eat, and also gave them to those who were with him?” And He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath. So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”

Mark 2:25–28

See also: Matthew 12:3–8 · Luke 6:3–5
In the Law: 22. Sabbath holiness and rest

14. It is lawful to do good on the Sabbaths: to save life, to lift out the sheep, to loose a daughter of Abraham from her bond.

He said to them, “Who among you, if he has one sheep and it falls into a pit on a Sabbath, will not grasp it and lift it out? How much more valuable, then, is a human being than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on Sabbaths.”

Matthew 12:11–12

See also: Mark 3:4 · Luke 6:9 · Luke 13:15–16 · Luke 14:3–5
In the Law: 22. Sabbath holiness and rest

15. Not to judge according to appearance, but to judge the righteous judgment: a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so that the Law of Moses may not be broken.

For this reason Moses has given you circumcision—not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers—and on a Sabbath you circumcise a person. If a person receives circumcision on a Sabbath so that the Law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with Me because I made a whole person well on a Sabbath? Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.”

John 7:22–24

See also: John 5:17
In the Law: 12. Circumcision in Abraham’s covenant · 22. Sabbath holiness and rest · 42. Impartial justice for poor people

Clean and Unclean, and the Tradition of the Elders

16. Not to set aside the commandment of God for the sake of tradition: honor your father and mother is not annulled by a vow of offering.

He said to them, “You set aside God’s commandment very well indeed, so that you may establish your tradition! For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Let whoever speaks evil of father or mother surely die.’ But you say, ‘If a person says to his father or mother, “Whatever benefit you might receive from me is Corban”—that is, a gift—’ you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother, making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. You do many similar things.”

Mark 7:9–13

See also: Matthew 15:3–9
In the Law: 23. Respecting and caring for parents · Exodus 21:16 (KJV 21:17) · 107. Vows, responsibility and household rules

17. Nothing that goes into a person from outside can defile him; what comes out of the heart defiles.

Transformed — dietary holiness and a cleansed heart

Read the ancient setting, New Testament development and continuing response: 61. Israel’s distinctions between clean and unclean food · 127. Food prohibited to Israel. What this study mark means.

Calling the crowd to Him again, He said to them, “Listen to Me, all of you, and understand. There is nothing outside a person that, by entering him, can defile him. Rather, the things coming out of a person are what defile the person.” When He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples asked Him about the parable. He said to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not grasp that everything entering a person from outside cannot defile him, because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—thus cleansing all foods. He said, “What comes out of a person is what defiles the person. For from within, out of people’s hearts, come evil reasonings, acts of sexual immorality, thefts, murders, adulteries, acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness. All these evil things come out from within and defile the person.”

Mark 7:14–23

See also: Matthew 15:10–20
In the Law: 61. Israel’s distinctions between clean and unclean food

Textual note: The Saints chapter follows a critical-text reading without Mark 7:16 in the main text; the quoted range preserves that reading.

18. To give as alms what is within, and everything is clean for you; woe to those who cleanse the outside of the cup.

And the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of plunder and wickedness. Fools! Did not the One who made the outside also make the inside? But give what is within as alms, and behold, everything is clean for you.

Luke 11:39–41

See also: Matthew 23:25–26

The Commandments and the One Thing Lacking

19. If you wish to enter life, keep the commandments: you shall not murder, commit adultery, steal, or bear false witness; honor your father and mother; love your neighbor as yourself.

He said to him, “Why do you ask Me about what is good? One is good. But if you wish to enter life, keep the commandments.” He said to Him, “Which ones?” Jesus said, “‘You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; honor father and mother’; and ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”

Matthew 19:17–19

See also: Mark 10:19 · Luke 18:20
In the Law: 24. The prohibition of murder · 25. Faithfulness in marriage · 26. Respect for another person’s property · 27. Truthful testimony about a neighbor · 23. Respecting and caring for parents · 79. Love of neighbor and refusal of revenge

20. One thing you lack: sell what you have, give to the poor, and come, follow Me.

Jesus looked at him, loved him, and said to him, “You lack one thing. Go, sell what you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

Mark 10:21

See also: Matthew 19:21 · Luke 18:22
In the Law: 132. Opening the hand to a poor neighbor

Temple, Offerings and Tithes

21. I desire mercy and not sacrifice: go and learn what this means.

Go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call righteous people, but sinners.”

Matthew 9:13

See also: Matthew 12:7

22. To the cleansed leper: show yourself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.

Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift Moses commanded as a testimony to them.”

Matthew 8:4

See also: Mark 1:44 · Luke 5:14 · Luke 17:14
In the Law: 63. Discharges, skin conditions and ritual cleansing

23. My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations; not to make the Father’s house a house of trade.

He taught and said to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”

Mark 11:17

See also: Matthew 21:13 · Luke 19:46 · John 2:16
In the Law: 90. Reverence for God’s sanctuary

24. The sons are free; yet, so as not to give offense, to pay the temple tax.

He says, “Yes.” And when he entered the house, Jesus spoke first to him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute: from their sons, or from strangers?” And when he said, “From strangers,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free. But lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; and when you open its mouth, you will find a stater. Take it and give it to them for Me and you.”

Matthew 17:25–27

In the Law: Exodus 30:11–16

25. To tithe mint, dill and cumin without leaving aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy and faithfulness.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint, dill, and cumin, but have left aside the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness! These you ought to have done without leaving those aside.

Matthew 23:23

See also: Luke 11:42
In the Law: Numbers 18:21–24 · 129. Tithes, worship and care for vulnerable people · 42. Impartial justice for poor people

26. The hour is coming when the Father will be worshiped neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem, but in spirit and truth.

Transformed — worship in spirit and truth

Read the ancient setting, New Testament development and continuing response: 124. Worship according to God’s instruction · 134. Three annual appearances before the Lord. What this study mark means.

Jesus said to her, “Believe Me, woman, an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews. But an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for the Father seeks such people to worship Him. God is spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth.”

John 4:21–24

In the Law: 124. Worship according to God’s instruction

Done to Be Seen

27. To do what the scribes and Pharisees say from Moses’ chair, but not according to their works; they broaden their phylacteries and lengthen their fringes to be seen.

saying, “The scribes and Pharisees have seated themselves in Moses’ chair. Therefore do and observe everything they tell you, but do not act according to their works, for they say and do not do. They bind heavy burdens, hard to carry, and lay them upon people’s shoulders, but they themselves are unwilling to move them with their finger. They do all their works to be seen by people. They broaden their phylacteries and enlarge their fringes. They love the foremost place at dinners and the foremost seats in the synagogues, greetings in the marketplaces, and being called ‘Rabbi’ by people.

Matthew 23:2–7

See also: Mark 12:38–40 · Luke 20:46–47
In the Law: 112. Keeping God’s words close and visible · 104. Tassels as reminders of the commandments

28. The widow’s two small coins: she put in more than all of them.

He called His disciples to Him and said to them, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury. For they all put in from their surplus, but she, from her need, put in everything she had—her whole livelihood.”

Mark 12:43–44

See also: Luke 21:3–4
In the Law: 132. Opening the hand to a poor neighbor
